I get sent a lot of first verses, and almost all of them have the same problem. They start with a feeling. I was so lost, I was broken, I did not know who I was any more. And I understand why, because that is the true thing, that is what the song is about. But a feeling is the conclusion, and you are giving me the conclusion in line one, so there is nothing left for me to do. Try this instead. Take the same verse and remove every word that names an emotion. What is left is usually a room, a time and an object, and those three things are the entire craft. The best opening line I read last year was six words long: the car was still running outside. Nobody said afraid. Nobody said leaving. And every single person who heard it knew both.

The twist is the most misunderstood thing in songwriting, because people hear the word and they think of a surprise ending, and that is not it at all. A surprise takes something away from you. A twist gives you something back. The difference is whether the line was available from the beginning. If I tell you at the end that the whole thing was a dream, you feel cheated, because there was nothing in the first two verses that could have told you. But if the coat was mentioned in verse one, and in the last line you find out she never took it off, you do not feel cheated. You feel clever, and you go back and listen again. That second listen is the entire commercial value of a twist. So here is the test I use. Write your last line first. Then go back into verse one and leave one small object there that makes the last line inevitable. If you cannot find the object, you do not have a twist. You have an ending.

Pedro says the verse sets a scene: the rain was falling and she was standing in the kitchen. Then he points out the events, in the past simple: she put the keys on the table and he asked where she had been. He notes that the lines are plain, with no emotion named anywhere. He says the images hint at everything and state nothing. He explains that the twist in the last line changes what came before it. Then he asks the other person what they noticed first.

While the radio was playing, the phone rang.
She did not answer him.
